name: security-audit-skill
description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings
one_liner: A set of instructions that turns an AI coding assistant into a security auditor, so it hunts for vulnerabilities in a codebase in careful stages and double-checks its own findings before reporting them.
buyer: A security engineer or engineering lead at a software company who wants cheap, repeatable first-pass security reviews before a human pentest or release.
business_use_cases: A startup with no dedicated security team runs this skill against its codebase before every major release to catch obvious vulnerabilities for free.
A security consultancy uses it as the first pass on a client engagement, so human pentesters spend their paid hours on the hard findings instead of the easy ones.
An open-source maintainer runs it on pull requests to flag risky changes (new network calls, loosened auth checks) before merging.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a hosted 'continuous audit' service that runs this skill against a company's repos on every release and emails a report.
Sell a few hours of expert review to interpret and prioritize the findings it produces.

steal_this: Wrap it in a GitHub Action that runs on every PR and posts the findings as a bot comment — sell it as a cheap automated security reviewer for small teams.
